name: Barabbas
overview: Barabbas was a male notorious prisoner known for being set free instead of the Messiah, as recorded in Matthew 27:16. Scripture does not provide information about his tribe or additional personal details beyond his infamous release. His role is unique in the Gospel narrative as the man chosen by the crowd to be freed in place of Jesus Christ.
namesAndTitles: The name Barabbas means 'son of the father,' a proper name mentioned in Matthew 27:16. This name, while common in form, contrasts poignantly with the identity of Jesus, the true Son of the Father, highlighting the irony of his release over the Messiah.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Barabbas beyond what is stated in his name and unique attribute. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Barabbas holds significant importance in the biblical narrative as the prisoner chosen by the crowd to be released instead of Jesus Christ, the Messiah. His release fulfills the Roman custom presented by Pilate and serves as a powerful symbol of the substitutionary nature of Christ's sacrifice. Through Barabbas, the Gospel highlights the rejection of the innocent Savior and the deliverance of a guilty man, underscoring the depth of Christ's atoning work.
